title: Bound the read, don't predict it
impact: Moonshot: rejected after adversarial review. The prototype confirmed exp 265's latency mechanism: removing worker dispatch cut the final candidate's hot point-read lanes by 60-65%, pages by 24-38%, a contended point read by 89.5%, and eight concurrent point reads by 69.8%. Its safety premise was false, however. A query returning one INTEGER, `length(randomblob(?))`, spent 26-28 ms inside one SQLite function opcode while remaining below the row, payload, VM-step, and per-turn admission limits; the candidate blocked the calling isolate for the whole interval while current main let its 1 ms timer run. The same gap covers busy/VFS waits, callbacks, cold preparation, and native TEXT scanning. Audit also found unsafe blanket replay, a cross-database schema-cache collision, false zero-value kill switches, an assert-only transfer invariant, and an evictable abort latch. No runtime change is kept. The focused routing harness and receipts remain as mechanism evidence, and a new opaque-work probe is the early rejection gate for any successor. The transferable rule is sharper than exp 265's: SQLite progress counters can request cancellation between selected VM operations, but they are not wall-time preemption; a stopwatch checked before opaque synchronous work is admission, not a bound.
